ai.title: /review switches to @thinker-gpt
ai.summary: CLI `/review` command and review-screen now spawn `@thinker-gpt` instead of `@GPT-5 Agent`. `command-registry.ts` and `review-screen.tsx` updated prompts; `slash-commands.ts` description changed. `base2.ts` adds `thinker-gpt` to agent list and restricts free-tier spawning. `thinker.ts` spawner prompt clarifies lack of tool access. `chatgpt-oauth.ts` adds `gpt-5.4` model mappings. `SPEC.md` updated.

eli5.text: Starting March 13, 2026, the `/review` command (which summons a coding review) now uses `@thinker-gpt` instead of `@GPT-5 Agent`. If you trigger `/review`, you'll be invoking a different reviewing system; the wording in prompts and help text was updated accordingly (e.g., the description now reads 'Review code changes with thinker-gpt'). Free tier users remain restricted from spawning this reviewer unless explicitly requested by you, and the system now warns that the thinker agent has no direct tool access and relies on context you provide first. If you looked at the interface today, you'd see the new naming and behavior live wherever the `/review` command or review screen appears.

ai.title: Add identifiers to Stripe billing metering requests
ai.summary: The `reportPurchasedCreditsToStripe` function now generates a UUID `identifier` if one is not provided, ensuring all Stripe metering events carry a unique ID. This identifier is passed to `stripeServer.billing.meterEvents.create` and used to construct the `idempotencyKey`. The `consumeCredits` function in `balance-calculator.ts` was updated to pass a `crypto.randomUUID()` as `eventId` to this reporting mechanism. This change affects the `packages/billing` subsystem, specifically `stripe-metering.ts` and `balance-calculator.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system charges you for credits you've used, it now tags each charge with a unique serial number before sending it to Stripe. That way, if the same charge gets sent twice, Stripe can tell they are the same one and won't bill you twice. The charge-recording part of your account and the part that reports your usage both add these serial numbers automatically. The change is live today and only affects how your usage is reported behind the scenes.

ai.title: ChatGPT OAuth connects via local callback server
ai.summary: CLI `/connect:chatgpt` now spins up local HTTP callback server at `localhost:1455` for automatic token exchange. Replaces manual paste flow. Auth URL adds `codex_cli_simplified_flow=true` and `originator=codex_cli_rs`. SDK routes ChatGPT OAuth requests through `chatgpt.com/backend-api` via custom fetch transformer converting Chat Completions to Responses API format. Token refresh failures no longer clear credentials, logging debug instead.

eli5.text: When you connect your ChatGPT account to the tool, it now opens a special local web page on your computer that automatically receives your login confirmation, so you no longer have to manually copy and paste a code. After you approve the connection in your browser, the tool exchanges that approval for an access token behind the scenes and signs you in directly. If the token can't be refreshed later, it stops trying instead of deleting your saved credentials, so you won't be logged out unexpectedly. The connection works by routing your requests through ChatGPT's backend, which translates the messages into the format ChatGPT expects.

ai.title: CLI ChatGPT connect UX improvements
ai.summary: ChatGPT connect flow in CLI now initiates OAuth automatically on entry, displays the auth URL, and shows a bordered panel with hover actions. `chat-input-bar.tsx` suppresses the input box during `connect:chatgpt` mode. `input-modes.ts` placeholder changed to 'authorizing in browser... press Escape to cancel'. `chatgpt-connect-banner.tsx` restructured to use `BORDER_CHARS` and track `authUrl`/`hovered` state, removing `BottomBanner` and `useChatStore` dependencies.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to connect to your ChatGPT account from the command-line app, it now goes straight to opening your web browser for the login step instead of showing a blank prompt where you had to paste a code. While that browser step is happening, the text area where you normally type disappears and a clearly bordered pop-up appears showing the login link and buttons you can hover over to click. The status message now reads "authorizing in browser... press Escape to cancel" so you know what to do if you change your mind. This only affects people who use the command-line tool and start the ChatGPT linking process.

ai.title: Thinker spawner prompt allows short prompts
ai.summary: Updated `spawnerPrompt` in `agents/thinker/thinker.ts` to inform the spawner that short prompts are acceptable. Change clarifies that the thinker agent sees the entire conversation history for context, removing the implication that all context must be manually gathered into the prompt.

eli5.text: You can now give the deep-thinking helper a much shorter instruction, because it automatically sees the whole conversation history you're having. Before this, you were expected to pack all the background into your prompt yourself; now the helper pulls in the context on its own, so you don't have to repeat everything. This change is live today.

ai.title: Add /plan command, unify prompt builders, clean up review UI
ai.summary: Added /plan slash command for spawning @thinker-gpt planning sessions, requiring ChatGPT OAuth in Freebuff mode. Centralized prompt construction into cli/src/commands/prompt-builders.ts for consistent /plan and /review behavior across direct args and interactive modes. Refactored cli/src/components/review-screen.tsx to remove embedded custom input state, delegating to chat-input-bar via new onCustom prop and router.ts input mode handling. ChatInputBar now renders mode labels (e.g., 'plan', 'review') using theme.info background.

eli5.text: You can now type a new "plan" command that asks the assistant to think through how to tackle whatever you're working on, like designing a new feature or solving a tricky problem. The setup looks cleaner: when the assistant offers to review your code, you can pick predefined options or type your own instructions, and the little status labels that show which mode you're in now appear right in the input box. One catch: the new /plan command only works if you've connected a ChatGPT account while in Freebuff mode, so if you haven't authorized ChatGPT yet, that command won't be available until you do.

ai.title: bash input mode switches from icon to label
ai.summary: The bash input mode in cli/src/utils/input-modes.ts now uses a text label `!` instead of an icon. The color changed from success to info, and widthAdjustment increased from 2 to 4 to accommodate the new label padding. This affects how the bash mode indicator is rendered in the CLI input prompt.

eli5.text: When you switch to bash mode in this CLI tool, the mode indicator in the input prompt will now show a text label "!" instead of just an icon. The label also changed from a green "success" color to a blue "info" color, and the spacing around it was widened to fit the new text label better. This makes the bash mode indicator more visually consistent with other input modes that use labels.

ai.title: Update slash command descriptions to specify GPT 5.4
ai.summary: Updated description strings for /plan and /review commands in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts to explicitly name GPT 5.4. Replaced generic 'GPT' references with the specific model version. Affects CLI help output and command picker metadata.

eli5.text: When you open the command line tool and look at the list of available actions like creating a plan or reviewing code, the short descriptions beside them now clearly state which version of the assistant they use instead of just saying GPT generically. This only affects what you see in the help text or command menu; the actual actions themselves still work the same way.

ai.title: Update what-models.mdx orchestrator model assignments
ai.summary: Updates the orchestrator model assignment table in web/src/content/advanced/what-models.mdx. Replaces GLM 4.7 with Minimax M2.5 for code editing, GPT-5.2 with GPT-5.4 for reasoning and review, and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite/Grok 4.1 Fast with Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite for file discovery, terminal commands, and web research. Removes the speculative decoding note for file rewrites.

eli5.text: The internal documentation that maps out which AI assistant handles which job has been quietly rewritten. The person who maintains or troubleshoots this setup will now see a different set of assistant assignments in the guide (for example, a different helper is now listed for code editing, reasoning, review, file hunting, running commands, and web research), and one explanatory note about how file rewrites work has been taken out. Nothing your experience as a user changes today from this; it's just an updated reference sheet behind the scenes.

ai.title: GPT-5.4 replaces GPT-5.2 in general agent and best-of-n selector
ai.summary: General agent and best-of-n selector2 now route `isGpt5` branches to `openai/gpt-5.4` instead of `openai/gpt-5.2`. This update ensures the default GPT-5 path uses the newer model version across core agent logic. Changes are localized to `agents/general-agent/general-agent.ts` and `agents/editor/best-of-n/best-of-n-selector2.ts`. Non-GPT-5 paths remain on `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` with no other behavioral shifts.

eli5.text: When you use the general-purpose assistant feature, it now taps into a newer version of its underlying large language model instead of the older one it was using before. That newer model also gets picked automatically by the system that compares multiple draft answers and selects the best one. You won't see a new button or setting, but responses routed through these features come from the updated model starting today. Other parts of the service that were already using different models continue unchanged.

eli5.text: If you use the free version of the assistant and live in Great Britain, Australia, or a number of European and Nordic countries such as Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands, Denmark, Germany, Finland, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Ireland, or Iceland, you can now sign in and use it from your location. Previously, free access was limited to users in the United States and Canada, so visitors from these newly included regions were blocked from the no-cost tier. This matters only if you are on the free plan: the system checks the country your internet connection appears to come from, and it now counts more countries as eligible. ai.title: Route openai models to direct API
ai.summary: OpenAI models now bypass OpenRouter via `handleOpenAIStream` and `isOpenAIDirectModel` in `web/src/llm-api/openai.ts`. Direct routing uses per-million-token cost maps for `gpt-5` through `gpt-5.4` variants plus `gpt-4o`/`gpt-4o-mini`, with `undici.Agent` enforcing 10-minute header timeouts for deep-thinking models. Scope limited to `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` and `web/src/llm-api/openai.ts`; free mode geo-block message generalized to 'Free mode is not available in your country.'

eli5.text: When you ask for a GPT-5, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3, GPT-5.4, GPT-4o, or GPT-4o-mini model, your request now goes straight to OpenAI instead of being sent through an intermediary service called OpenRouter. You may notice that responses from these models can take longer to start, especially for the GPT-5.x versions, because the system now waits up to 10 minutes for the first response before timing out. If you use the free version in a country where it's not available, the error message you see is now simply: "Free mode is not available in your country." These changes are live today for anyone using the chat completions API endpoint.

ai.title: Hide /plan in regular codebuff
ai.summary: Added FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMANDS and FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMAND_IDS sets containing 'plan' in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts respectively. These sets filter out the /plan command when IS_FREEBUFF is false. Regular codebuff no longer exposes /plan in its command registry or slash command list.

eli5.text: When you open the CLI assistant, the /plan command has been removed from the list of available commands. You won't see it appear in auto-complete suggestions or be able to invoke it through the regular interface. This change takes effect immediately for users without access to that specific command set.

ai.title: CLI @agent references use id not displayName
ai.summary: Agent mention replacement in cli/src/chat.tsx now inserts @${selected.id} instead of @${selected.displayName}. Suggestion engine in cli/src/hooks/use-suggestion-engine.ts sets label to agent.id, clears description, and maps highlight indices to idHighlightIndices. Affects CLI chat surface. Removes displayName from visible suggestion metadata and reference output.

eli5.text: When you reference an agent in the CLI chat, it now uses the agent's unique ID (like @agent-123) instead of its display name (like @My Custom Agent). This means the autocomplete suggestions you see while typing also show the agent's ID as the label, and the description (which used to show the ID) is now blank. If you look at the chat now, agent mentions will appear as short IDs rather than whatever name you might have given them.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.10
ai.summary: The CLI release manifest in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` increments the packaged binary version from 0.0.9 to 0.0.10 as part of the release-bump commit. This metadata-only change accompanies the cumulative set of user-visible features and fixes documented in the 0.0.10 release updates (model routing shifts, ChatGPT OAuth, `/plan` and `/review` command refinements, free-mode geo expansion, and Fireworks deployment tweaks), freezing that work into the next distributed CLI build.
ai.evidence: Commit 65327046 modifies only `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `0.0.9` to `0.0.10` with a single-line diff.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.10 expands access and improves the coding agent experience across the web and CLI. Free mode is now available to users in 15 English-speaking and European countries (including the UK, Australia, and select Nordic nations), so more developers worldwide can use the agent without a paid subscription. The model lineup has been refreshed: GPT-5.4 replaces GPT-5.2 across core agent logic, review sessions now run on a dedicated @thinker-gpt agent, and a new /plan command lets users kick off planning sessions with ChatGPT OAuth integration. ChatGPT OAuth setup is now smoother, with automatic browser authentication via a local callback server and a revamped in-terminal connect flow that shows the auth URL and hoverable actions without requiring manual token pasting. Additional improvements include better routing for OpenAI models going straight to their source, disabling non-essential custom model deployments during scaling issues, and a cleaner UI with updated command labels and a new bash input indicator. Upgrading gives you broader regional access, faster and clearer OAuth onboarding, newer model versions, and a more polished command palette experience.

ai.title: Add useCustomDeployment flag to createFireworksRequestWithFallback
ai.summary: The `createFireworksRequestWithFallback` function in `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts` now accepts an optional `useCustomDeployment` boolean parameter. This overrides the global `FIREWORKS_USE_CUSTOM_DEPLOYMENT` constant, defaulting to the constant's value if unspecified. The change allows per-request control over whether to attempt deployment fallbacks during business hours.

eli5.text: You can now tell the system, on a per-request basis, whether to try falling back to a different model version during weekday business hours, instead of letting a single global setting decide for every request. The setting still defaults to whatever the global default is, so existing behavior doesn't change unless you choose to override it for a specific request. This gives finer control over how the assistant handles traffic when the primary model is busiest.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 0.0.11
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version is bumped from 0.0.10 to 0.0.11 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`. This release-bump commit ships alongside the earlier same-day changes, including the `useCustomDeployment` flag for `createFireworksRequestWithFallback` in `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts`, allowing per-request control over deployment fallbacks. No other files are modified in this commit.
ai.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` increments the `version` field from `0.0.10` to `0.0.11`, marking a release-bump commit with no other file changes.

eli5.text: This release introduces a new option that lets you choose whether the app should automatically switch to a backup AI service if your main one takes too long, and you can now pick that behavior for individual requests instead of only setting it once for everything. The update gives you more control over how and when those automatic failovers happen, so you can decide on a case-by-case basis whether to wait for your preferred service or jump to a backup right away. Upgrading means you get a smarter, more flexible way to handle occasional slowdowns or hiccups from your chosen AI provider.
